concepts.name: spec
concepts.meaning: A markdown file (`# Name`, intent paragraph, optional `## works when`, `## invariants`, `## refutations`, `## why`, `## zones`, `## architecture`, `## addresses`, `## relies on`, `## guarantee bindings`) whose presence makes its folder a component; the primary object the whole harness derives from.
concepts.overlap_note: 'node' (walk.ts, README) and 'component' (everywhere else) name the same thing: a folder that owns a spec.

concepts.name: component
concepts.meaning: A folder containing a *.spec.md; the unit of ownership (deepest spec dir owns each file), of claims, of coverage, of co-change locality and of every reading surface.
concepts.overlap_note: Index calls it an 'organ', Structure a 'stack'/'card', types.ts a GraphNode of kind 'component', walk.ts a 'node'.

concepts.name: intent
concepts.meaning: The first paragraph after the spec's H1: the derivable one-sentence statement of what a component is for, shown in CLAUDE.md, the outline, the panel and Structure cards.
concepts.overlap_note: Scope stores it as a `description` asset; the root architecture `purpose` declaration is a separate, explicitly authored project-level intent.

concepts.name: prose (the what)
concepts.meaning: Derivable, regenerable documentation of what code does, as opposed to why; docblock text before `@why` and spec text outside the recognised sections.

concepts.name: why (rationale)
concepts.meaning: Authored, protected rationale that the graph cannot derive; verify never generates it (an AUTHOR job instead), why-lint checks it anchors to invariants, Scope stores it as a `rationale` asset.

concepts.name: claim
concepts.meaning: One bullet under `## works when`, written in the phrasebook grammar; verify grades each claim pass/fail/skip every run so a rotted doc goes red. A line matching no form is skipped, never red.

concepts.name: claim form
concepts.meaning: One entry of the ordered CLAIM_FORMS registry (typechecks, exists, imports, responds, passes test, boundary, coverage, lives in, parity, conforms to); first match wins, and each form carries a tier and an evaluator.

concepts.name: phrasebook
concepts.meaning: The rendered table of claim forms (name, tier, grammar, example), derived from CLAIM_FORMS into README and the terminal.

concepts.name: claim kind
concepts.meaning: A project-declared category a claim may carry as a trailing `[kind]`; policy `pin` gates normally, `warn` gates but reports, an undeclared kind is red. Off unless configured.
concepts.overlap_note: Not to be confused with graph node kind, asset kind, journal record kind, or scaffold kind.

concepts.name: invariant
concepts.meaning: A named property a component upholds, declared under `## invariants`; every one must be anchored by a `boundary`/`coverage`/`parity` claim or coverage fails. The promise graph renders the anchored form as a gate, Scope as a guarantee, Structure as a promise.
concepts.overlap_note: Four layer names for one authored thing (invariant/gate/guarantee/contract) with no journal decision choosing between them; the Scope Guarantees view is even titled 'Invariants'.

concepts.name: boundary claim
concepts.meaning: `boundary "<invariant>" at <chokepoint> [over <enumeration>] [crossing a -> b] [via test|guard "<oracle>"]` — asserts the four-part anatomy of a self-enforcing boundary and anchors the invariant for the coverage gate.
concepts.overlap_note: The promise graph calls a boundary claim a gate; guarantees.ts hashes it into a g-… guarantee reference; conventions.ts calls it a contract.

concepts.name: chokepoint
concepts.meaning: The one code symbol all paths to the protected thing cross; a boundary claim fails until the symbol exists in the code graph.
concepts.overlap_note: Atlas transitions and contracts are keyed by the same chokepoint symbols, spelled again in config.

concepts.name: oracle
concepts.meaning: The named test (or source guard) whose pass is the evidence behind a claim; resolved by exact describe title through the batch report, serial runner, or static index.
concepts.overlap_note: 'oracle' also names the machine that grades (meta-oracle, totality oracle, static oracle) — the word covers both the test and the analyzer of the test.

concepts.name: via guard
concepts.meaning: The escape hatch verb: the oracle must still run and pass, but the live-domain meta-oracle is skipped because the oracle asserts a source property or non-domain behaviour; every guard row carries a human-eye flag.
concepts.overlap_note: 'guard' also means a load-bearing guard function in the conventions detector — a different thing.

concepts.name: meta-oracle
concepts.meaning: Static analysis of a `via test` oracle's own source that classifies how it iterates its domain; LIVE passes, LITERAL/NO-ITERATION/NOT-FOUND fail. Runs even under --fast.
concepts.overlap_note: Overlaps with the totality gate (totality.ts), a stricter, separate admission for claims that say 'total'.

concepts.name: domain floor
concepts.meaning: An `expect(domain.length >= n)` in an oracle so a live domain that collapses to empty fails loud instead of passing vacuously; the meta-oracle annotates its absence but never fails on it.
concepts.overlap_note: 'floor' also names the non-vacuity floor of verify and the advisory floors (thresholds) — three unrelated floors.

concepts.name: enumeration
concepts.meaning: The concrete source-owned collection a totality or parity claim is total over; must be a symbol in the graph and (for 'total' claims) a nonempty literal const/enum directly iterated by the oracle.
concepts.overlap_note: Redundancy calls the same thing an 'enumerated domain' spelled at a 'site'.

concepts.name: totality
concepts.meaning: The promise that an oracle covers every member of a declared domain; a claim whose invariant or oracle says 'total' must name its enumeration and the oracle must directly iterate it, or the claim fails.
concepts.overlap_note: 'totality-checked' is also the name of enforcement-ladder tier 2, which applies to any oracle-backed crossing, not only ones that say 'total'.

concepts.name: coverage claim
concepts.meaning: `coverage "<subject>" at <chokepoint> residual "<what is NOT covered>" [via …]` — the honest verb for a set the world defines; it buys silence from the meta-oracle at the price of naming its residual.
concepts.overlap_note: Name collision: 'coverage' is also verify's coverage gate (claims present, invariants anchored, why present) and 'coverage %' in the receipts/scope docs.

concepts.name: crossing
concepts.meaning: The declarative clause on a boundary/coverage claim naming which pair of trust zones the gate separates; promise-graph topology, never a runtime check.
concepts.overlap_note: Atlas 'transitions' (config, between charts) and claim 'crossings' (spec, between zones) are two spellings of 'a chokepoint between trust regions'.

concepts.name: zone
concepts.meaning: A declared trust region from the entry spec's `## zones` (declared order = trust order, `inside` nests); components declare residence with `lives in`, gates declare crossings between zones.
concepts.overlap_note: Zones (spec) and atlas charts (config) are both 'trust domains'; docs/scope.md insists they are different concepts, but both carry the same idea.

concepts.name: lives in (residence)
concepts.meaning: `lives in <zone>` declares which trust zone a component resides in so cross-component imports can be graded same-zone / covered / naked; verify only checks well-formedness.

concepts.name: parity claim
concepts.meaning: `parity "<invariant>" over <domain> between <fnA> and <fnB> via test "<oracle>"` — two functions declared projections of one enumerated domain that must agree; anchors an invariant like a boundary.
concepts.overlap_note: Redundancy is described as 'the undeclared half of parity'.

concepts.name: projection
concepts.meaning: One of the two functions a parity claim declares must agree over a domain; also used loosely for any pure derivation (scope model, structure model, orient projection).
concepts.overlap_note: Heavily overloaded word: parity projection, 'trusted projection' of the journal, Scope 'projection', orient 'projection'.

concepts.name: deterministic claims
concepts.meaning: The fast-tier forms that need no runner: typechecks shells the typecheck command; exists and imports check the file tree. The README warns a spec full of them is 'coherent and worthless'.

concepts.name: responds claim
concepts.meaning: A live-tier claim that fetches a URL; unreachable is a skip, wrong status/body is a fail.

concepts.name: passes test claim
concepts.meaning: A claim that a named test passes; refuses the word 'totality' because it names no chokepoint, so it cannot name an enumeration.

concepts.name: dictionary word
concepts.meaning: A named pattern file (`# Word`, intent, `## commitments` claim list) that a component `conforms to`; commitments are evaluated against the conforming component, red-not-skip, and propagate on edit.
concepts.overlap_note: README notes words are parameterless so most commitments are global 'documentation, not discrimination'.

concepts.name: commitment
concepts.meaning: One claim line inside a dictionary word; must match a claim form or the word goes red.

concepts.name: refutation
concepts.meaning: `<invariant>: <what was broken> -> <what was seen>` — the recorded experiment in which an invariant's oracle actually went red; verify reports coverage over it but never fails on it.

concepts.name: architecture section
concepts.meaning: A spec section of JSON-object bullets declaring purpose, entrances and relationships with stable ids; parsed strictly, unresolved endpoints stay visible as issues.

concepts.name: purpose declaration
concepts.meaning: The architecture bullet that states what the project is for, shown above the Structure canvas; distinct from the root spec's narrower intent.
concepts.overlap_note: Overlaps with the root component's intent; both are 'what the project does'.

concepts.name: entrance
concepts.meaning: An architecture declaration naming where a human or agent enters the system (label, component, optional file/symbol anchor); rendered as external arrows into stacks.
concepts.overlap_note: Not the same as `entryDir` / the entry component, which is a graph root, not an execution entrance (the thesis says so explicitly).

concepts.name: architectural relationship
concepts.meaning: A spec-owned assessed relationship between two components with a label and rationale; the only kind of arrow the default Structure map draws (imports never qualify).
concepts.overlap_note: Structure docs call these 'handoffs'; the work ledger also has a 'handoff' event — unrelated meanings.

concepts.name: guarantee link
concepts.meaning: Spec-owned JSON bullets: a provider's `## addresses` maps a g-… claim to a taxonomy obligation via an assessment revision; a consumer's `## relies on` names a provider's claim it depends on (direct-import grade). `guarantees --check` checks link integrity only.
concepts.overlap_note: 'relies on' (declared, spec) vs 'reliance' (derived from imports in the promise graph) are two different things called nearly the same name; Structure draws the declared one as a 'relied-on tab'.

concepts.name: guarantee binding
concepts.meaning: Spec-owned adoption of a catalog definition: definition id + digest, local g-… claim, subject, assessor, applicability rationale, parameter values, exclusions, falsifier and SHA-256 evidence pins; verify retains bound inputs so support expires when inputs change.
concepts.overlap_note: Name collision with platform 'Bindings' (types.ts: Cloudflare stores/entities/vars) — same word, unrelated.

concepts.name: ownership
concepts.meaning: The rule that the deepest spec'd ancestor directory owns a file; `null` when nothing owns it (represented, not fabricated). Also the parent/child containment of components, which is never an import.
concepts.overlap_note: 'owner' also means the work order owner session and the guarantee's canonical owner component.

concepts.name: graph
concepts.meaning: The one derivation every renderer and verify consumes: components, files, symbols, claims, import edges, platform bindings, built by buildGraph from the spec tree plus adapters. No second walk anywhere.
concepts.overlap_note: Decompose splits it into 'Intent graph' (spec tree) and 'Structure graph' (imports); atlas calls it the 'derived-model' chart.

concepts.name: symbol
concepts.meaning: A function/method/class/const captured by the language adapter; the address space boundary claims, parity claims, contracts and taxonomy subjects resolve against.

concepts.name: import edge
concepts.meaning: A resolved module import between two files in the graph; the basis of reliance in the promise graph, of context closure in economy, of hubs in decompose, and explicitly NOT an architectural arrow in Structure.
concepts.overlap_note: Promise graph turns a cross-component import into a 'reliance'; Scope catalog also calls its `relies on` relation 'reliance'.

concepts.name: import alias
concepts.meaning: Config-declared exact or trailing-star module mappings that resolve only to a unique walked file; malformed or escaping declarations refuse.

concepts.name: language adapter
aliases: instrument arm row (SURFACE_LANGUAGES, SITE_LANGUAGES, SINK_LANGUAGES, ORACLE_LANGUAGES)
concepts.meaning: How coherence reads a language: symbols, imports and docblocks through a wasm grammar plus capture queries; built-in packs are data (queries, patterns, named strategies), never code, and a project may supply its own module.
concepts.overlap_note: 'pack' means language pack here and taxonomy pack (core/simulation) in taxonomy — unrelated.

concepts.name: pack purity
aliases: a pack is data never code
concepts.meaning: The rule that every built-in language table carries queries, patterns and named strategies only; a guard sweeps for function-valued fields.

concepts.name: platform adapter
concepts.meaning: How coherence reads infrastructure config: Cloudflare wrangler plus direct Env types produce store/entity nodes and declared variable names; deployment values are unrepresentable.
concepts.overlap_note: 'Bindings' here collides with guarantee bindings; Scope calls the result 'resource' assets.

concepts.name: entry component
concepts.meaning: The component at `entryDir` (`.` by default); the only spec whose `## zones` has topology authority, and Structure's project frame when it owns children.
concepts.overlap_note: Not an execution entrance; the thesis warns against conflating entryDir with an entrance.

concepts.name: coherence root
concepts.meaning: The directory containing coherence.config.json; its presence is the declaration that walking commands may run here, so a configless run refuses instead of walking a home directory.
concepts.overlap_note: Distinct from the host project root (claudeProjectRoot/codexProjectRoot) and the package root.

concepts.name: config
concepts.meaning: The project's declared settings over defaults: runner commands, language/platform, adoption of ratchets/atlas/contracts data, thresholds; an empty `{}` is complete; unparseable refuses.

concepts.name: tooling group
concepts.meaning: Config path prefixes demoted to a 'tooling' group in the outline so build scripts do not read as product structure.

concepts.name: file stats / claimed files
concepts.meaning: The one on-disk read of line counts and content hashes every measurer uses, and the one definition of which files a claim blesses (path-suffix match, at most one file per token).

concepts.name: undocumented symbol
concepts.meaning: An exported symbol with no docblock; surfaced as an advisory job ranked hottest-first, never red.

concepts.name: evolution graph
concepts.meaning: The third graph: git history read once per process (non-merge commits with touched files, net-LOC deltas), filtered to concern-carrying commits, consumed by decompose, drift, mass, economy, atlas heat and verify.

concepts.name: verify
concepts.meaning: The command that grades every claim, the narrative chain and coverage, in a fast (deterministic) or full (live/executable) tier, files a status record, emits jobs, and optionally writes a receipt.
concepts.overlap_note: 'verify' is also an orient heading and a consequence relation ('verifies').

concepts.name: verify run tier
concepts.meaning: Which claims a verify run executes: --fast runs structural claims, typechecks, anchoring, meta-oracle and static existence; the full run adds responds probes and test oracles. Tiers age independently in the status record.
concepts.overlap_note: Three unrelated 'tier' vocabularies coexist: run tier (fast/full), claim-form tier (deterministic/live/executable/hybrid), enforcement-ladder tier (1/2/3).

concepts.name: claim tier
concepts.meaning: The tier field of a claim form saying what evidence it needs; hybrid forms mix a deterministic part (anchoring, symbol lookup, meta-oracle) with an executable oracle.
concepts.overlap_note: See verify run tier and tier (enforcement ladder).

concepts.name: verdict
concepts.meaning: What a gate is permitted to say about one claim: pass, fail or skip with a detail; recorded per claim in the status record and rendered as lights, chips and Scope claim-result assets.
concepts.overlap_note: The panel's 'light' adds stale/not-run/dialect-gap marks derived from the same verdicts.

concepts.name: dialect gap
concepts.meaning: A claim line matching no form: skipped rather than red, so a typo'd verb is a silent no-op; the panel gives it its own mark and the promise graph grades it U.

concepts.name: anchoring
concepts.meaning: The relation between an invariant and the boundary/coverage/parity claim that enforces it; the coverage gate refuses unanchored invariants, and novelty/signal count 'anchors added'.
concepts.overlap_note: 'anchor' also names an entrance anchor (file/symbol address) and atlas `anchoredBy`.

concepts.name: coverage gate
concepts.meaning: Verify's meta-claims over the graph: every component carries claims and a `## why`, and every declared invariant is anchored; a failure reds the run.
concepts.overlap_note: Collides with the `coverage` claim verb and with 'refutation coverage' (a report line, never red).

concepts.name: never-red advisory
concepts.meaning: Claims green on 3+ runs that have never been red and carry no refutation are flagged as possibly unfalsifiable; backed by everFailed/lastFailAt in the status record.

concepts.name: holding cost
concepts.meaning: What a run pays to keep each claim true: per-claim duration with the clock that produced it, summed (never blended), filed run-level in the status record.

concepts.name: oracle execution mode
concepts.meaning: How the executable tier runs: from a supplied report, one batched whole-suite run (configured or derived), or one runner boot per claim (only when named); an unrecognized runner refuses loudly.

concepts.name: test runner
concepts.meaning: The project-configured command coherence shells to answer executable claims, plus the harness's own node:test shim that resolves a name to its owning file so a vanished name exits nonzero.

concepts.name: testMatch
concepts.meaning: A regex the runner output must contain for a serial pass to count, because runners exit 0 when a name filter matched nothing; unnecessary for batched claims.

concepts.name: vanished oracle
concepts.meaning: A claim citing a test name nothing owns; batch mode and the static floor make it its own red verdict rather than a pass.

concepts.name: static oracle index
concepts.meaning: A zero-execution scan of test source that proves a named oracle exists (skip) or is statically absent (red); dynamic titles make absence UNKNOWN.

concepts.name: serial canary
aliases: a checker never seen to fail
concepts.meaning: Once per serial verify, run the runner with a name that exists nowhere and require it to fail; a runner that passes cannot filter by name and is refused.
concepts.overlap_note: 'canary' also names the live swarm canary in README validation and the PostToolUse startup canary.

concepts.name: non-vacuity floor
concepts.meaning: Before grading, prove a surface exists: a run deriving zero claims while the record remembers a graded surface refuses; a ratchet refuses to pin an empty reading over a live baseline.
concepts.overlap_note: See 'floor' overload in domain floor.

concepts.name: adoption ladder
concepts.meaning: What verify prints on a project with no record and no claims instead of a green: the named adoption state and one re-runnable next action per run.

concepts.name: narrative evidence chain
concepts.meaning: Prose statements pinned to evidence files; verify hashes the evidence and flips statements to pending (job emitted) or broken (hard fail); verdicts re-pin them.
concepts.overlap_note: Scope docs call these 'narrative verification' exclusions from receipts.

concepts.name: verify jobs
concepts.meaning: The list verify emits for a subagent: judge statements, generate derivable docs/claims, or author a missing why; ranked by churn heat.

concepts.name: verdicts file
concepts.meaning: The subagent's answers to VERIFY jobs (`{id, supported, reason, corrected}`) that verify records mechanically; the judge and the notary are deliberately separate parties.

concepts.name: verify scope
concepts.meaning: Restricting a run to components whose files changed (plus conformers of an edited dictionary word); scoped runs replace only what they touched in the record.
concepts.overlap_note: 'scope' is also the Scope reading surface, work read/write scopes, and decision scope fields — four unrelated uses.

concepts.name: receipt
concepts.meaning: An immutable, content-addressed record of one verify run (raw observations, before/after input manifests, executor and configuration fingerprints) that can be bound to a work order and cited by a `verifies` consequence edge. Local unattested testimony, not proof.
concepts.overlap_note: Overlaps with the status record (rolling, merged) — receipts exist precisely because status cannot identify one run.

concepts.name: input manifest / input grade
concepts.meaning: The bounded set of bytes a receipt binds (tracked and untracked source, index provenance, effective config, executor id), with named exclusions (status scratch, receipts, jobs, work/consequence ledgers).

concepts.name: guarantee reading
concepts.meaning: A boundary claim addressed by a stable hash of its owner directory and full parsed boundary, joined to its recorded oracle verdict, taxonomy obligations and explicit links; the unit `guarantees`, Scope's Guarantees view and guarantee links refer to.
concepts.overlap_note: This is the 'guarantee' layer name for an invariant+boundary pair; the guarantee catalog's 'guarantee definitions' are a different, project-independent thing with the same word.

concepts.name: guarantee catalog
aliases: promise / appliesWhen / parameters / excludes / falsifier / demoteWhen / distinctFrom / example
concepts.meaning: A project-independent reference catalog of 36 scoped guarantee definitions with applicability, binding parameters, exclusions, falsifiers, demotion criteria and pinned PostHog examples; lookup loads no project and activates nothing.
concepts.overlap_note: Shares the `guarantee:` id namespace with taxonomy suggestions (`guarantee:G-…`), yet README says catalog ids cannot be used as taxonomy obligations — two populations, one prefix.

concepts.name: falsifier
concepts.meaning: The catalog definition's described way to break the guarantee; Scope drafts a `coherence conjecture` challenge command from it for a binding (draft only, never recorded by the browser).
concepts.overlap_note: A falsifier is the catalog's counterpart of a refutation: the former is a planned break, the latter an observed one.

concepts.name: obligation
concepts.meaning: What a component owes by its assessed role: a taxonomy-suggested guarantee that stays unverified until an explicit `## addresses` link maps it to a local claim; never a verdict.
concepts.overlap_note: Three 'obligations': taxonomy suggestions (implemented), the proposed `## obligations` spec section (docs/code-contracts-lessons-design.md), and doctrine/regulator 'obligations' (a rule owed an action).

concepts.name: obligations section (proposed)
concepts.meaning: A designed-but-unimplemented spec section for rules that cannot yet go red, inheriting downward, diffed by log, promotable to an invariant; proposed alongside `coherence governs` and `coherence review`.
concepts.overlap_note: Would add a third meaning of 'obligation'; the design doc itself says vocabulary must be reconciled.

concepts.name: decision journal
concepts.meaning: Append-only, per-session JSONL of what agents chose, rejected, wondered, could not do, and escalated; merged into one timeline; it gates nothing by design.
concepts.overlap_note: 'journal' names the whole record, the `journal` live-read command, and the `journal` Scope view; 'decisions' names both the read command and the storage folder holding all nine record kinds.

concepts.name: decision
concepts.meaning: A point where the work could have gone more than one way and someone picked; recorded with what was chosen, what was rejected, and why, before moving on.

concepts.name: --over (rejected alternative)
concepts.meaning: The repeatable list of what a decision rejected; the cache entry for the search that need not be re-run, and the field gate-shaped designs drop.

concepts.name: blocked
concepts.meaning: What an agent could NOT do and why; first-class, renders in its own section, but is historical testimony with no close lifecycle (unlike a blocked work state).
concepts.overlap_note: Collides with the `blocked` work state; orient treats journal blockage as history, work blockage as live.

concepts.name: conjecture
concepts.meaning: What surprised an agent, with candidate explanations (the instrument-is-wrong candidate is injected) and the test that would settle it; open conjectures render above standing decisions.

concepts.name: resolution
concepts.meaning: An append pointing at a conjecture that closes it with what the discriminating test showed; refuses ids that are not conjectures.

concepts.name: dismissal
concepts.meaning: Retiring a conjecture without answering it; its own record kind and section, never raised again by an advisory. Precedence: retraction > resolution > dismissal.

concepts.name: retraction
concepts.meaning: Withdrawing a decision or conjecture by appending a record that points at it; crosses session files; a retracted conjecture may be raised again.

concepts.name: escalation
concepts.meaning: A record that a person must see something before anyone proceeds; heads every journal read and orient until a human appends an acknowledgement; gates nothing mechanically.
defined_in: RELEASE-NOTES.md#Unreleased — the route to a human
concepts.overlap_note: Distinct from `blocked` by who must act: what the agent could not do vs what no agent may decide.

concepts.name: acknowledgement
concepts.meaning: A human's record of having seen an escalation and what they decided — the only thing that clears one; retracting it reopens the escalation.

concepts.name: observed metric
concepts.meaning: A harness-reported measurement with the project's own band; outside the band and unexplained it opens at most one conjecture per label; coming back inside resolves nothing.

concepts.name: session record
concepts.meaning: The journal row a hook writes when a session opens, attributing later rows; withheld from the Scope journal view but counted.

concepts.name: journal id
aliases: def-… / e-… / wrk-… / lnk-… / t-… ids
concepts.meaning: Ids are pointers minted from a record's content (fields joined on NUL), so a retraction or resolution can name a row across files and a retry dedupes; each ledger has its own prefix.
defined_in: README.md#Storage: one append-only file per agent session

concepts.name: session
concepts.meaning: The exact writer identity every ledger write is attributed to and the filename it appends to; random for a hook, derived for a hand-typed command, hashed when names alias.

concepts.name: agent / job attribution
concepts.meaning: Caller-supplied labels (not authenticated identities) stored on every row: which agent wrote it and which job/branch it belonged to.
concepts.overlap_note: 'job' is used both as the journal attribution field (branch name) and for verify's inference 'jobs' — unrelated.

concepts.name: branch / commit provenance
concepts.meaning: The git branch, short commit and dirty bit captured on journal rows, status sections, receipts and defects so a reader can date every claim; null means git could not answer.

concepts.name: decision wire v2 fields
concepts.meaning: Optional structured fields that make a decision addressable by the swarm: the exact question (subject), the authority grade, the work it belongs to and machine-addressable scope. They do not infer each other.
defined_in: README.md#Two journal reads, two trust contracts
concepts.overlap_note: Decision `scope` (component/file/symbol) is another meaning of 'scope'.

concepts.name: decision position
concepts.meaning: Derived per subject from explicit fields: differing local proposals need ratification, a stronger authority ratifies, ties at the top stay contested; prose similarity and recency never decide.
concepts.overlap_note: 'authority' is split into decision authority (whose choice ratifies) and work authority (who may act) — deliberately, but with one word.

concepts.name: trusted projection vs tolerant read
concepts.meaning: Two contracts over every ledger: human renders keep whatever rows survive and show damage; verdict-bearing consumers (signal, orient, regulate) refuse the whole population on one malformed, displaced or conflicting row, and consult Git HEAD when zero rows survive.
defined_in: README.md#Two journal reads, two trust contracts

concepts.name: compaction
concepts.meaning: Folding committed session files into one per (branch, month) without changing what `decisions` prints; skips uncommitted, recent, or edited files.

concepts.name: journal stream
concepts.meaning: The chronological, live, per-stream read of the same record, deduped on record identity so appends and compaction folds neither drop nor duplicate an entry.

concepts.name: journal feed
concepts.meaning: Opt-in delivery of peer journal entries into an agent's context at prompt and tool boundaries as bounded, escaped, attributed data, with per-session cursors that only advance on flushed output and a dead-holder-recoverable lock.

concepts.name: defect
concepts.meaning: An agent's assessed conclusion that behaviour violated an expectation, with the evidence that made it a defect and affected files; append-only, content-addressed, no repair lifecycle.
concepts.overlap_note: Also the calibration outcome label `defect` (clean | defect) — same word, different record.

concepts.name: experiment
concepts.meaning: A frozen falsifiable plan (hypothesis, predicted reading surface, inert actions, observable criteria, evidence cursors) closed later with evidence for every id; the outcome is derived, never supplied.

concepts.name: telemetry scope
concepts.meaning: The label an experiment close gives its trace and activity windows naming the strongest attribution the frozen rows actually prove.
concepts.overlap_note: Same vocabulary as calibration's attribution and hook status's parent-fallback.

concepts.name: status record
aliases: verify / atlas / drift / mass / economy sections
concepts.meaning: The persistent report every instrument files instead of only printing: per-claim verdicts with sticky red history, tier grades, trajectories, cost; each section stamped with time, commit and dirty bit. Merge rules: a skip never clobbers a verdict, scoped runs replace only what they touched.
defined_in: README.md#The status record and the panel
concepts.overlap_note: Only 5 of 51 commands write it, which is why `due` cannot report the other 46.

concepts.name: freshness
concepts.meaning: Whether a recorded reading still describes the tree: a verdict from another commit is stale, a taxonomy assessment whose subject bytes changed is stale, a receipt is current only at the same HEAD with no material change.
concepts.overlap_note: Spelled 'stale', 'expired', 'current', 'currency' across layers for one idea.

concepts.name: premise lease
concepts.meaning: The mechanically answerable part of 'is this cached decision still true': do the repository addresses it named still resolve? Authored `files` are gate-grade, prose paths advisory.

concepts.name: calibration sample
concepts.meaning: A per-session comparison of economy's predicted one-hop context against explicitly traced reads for a patch, labeled later with an outcome; a lower bound, never causal proof.

concepts.name: read trace
concepts.meaning: The transient per-session record of explicit read/write paths from tool events, carrying host, transport, bundle hash and attribution; feeds calibration and experiments.

concepts.name: activity row
concepts.meaning: The per-session append-only record of hook traffic used to answer whether the installed launcher ever reached the body and what a session is doing; internally inconsistent rows count as damage.

concepts.name: work order
aliases: objective / success criteria / constraints / non-goals / risk / authority / owner / parent / dependencies / read+write scopes
concepts.meaning: An append-only record of intent and authority for coordinated agent work: frozen at open, advanced by predecessor-checked events, owned by one exact session; it coordinates but never spawns or executes.

concepts.name: work state
concepts.meaning: The lifecycle of a work order and its derived readiness; activation and completion wait on dependencies, cancelled is the terminal non-success that satisfies nothing.
concepts.overlap_note: `blocked` here is live scheduler state; the journal's `blocked` is history.

concepts.name: work event
concepts.meaning: One content-addressed event appended to the writer's file, pointing at its predecessor so two writers advancing the same predecessor create competing history that the strict reader refuses.

concepts.name: handoff
concepts.meaning: The only way work ownership moves: an event naming the next exact session/agent pair.
concepts.overlap_note: Structure docs use 'handoff' for an architectural relationship arrow — unrelated.

concepts.name: work authority
concepts.meaning: Who granted a work order and within what plain-language limit; answers who may act, separately from decision authority (whose choice ratifies).
concepts.overlap_note: 'boundary' here is an authority limit, not a boundary claim.

concepts.name: write scope / collision
concepts.meaning: Declared path scopes on work orders; two runnable orders with overlapping write scopes are a collision, an overlap serialized behind a dependency stays potential. The ledger reports, it cannot prevent.

concepts.name: synthesis
concepts.meaning: A parent work order closes only when every live child is terminal and names each completed direct child it synthesized; there is no separate checkbox.

concepts.name: consequence
aliases: relation (authorizes | implements | produces | evaluates | verifies | supports | contradicts | reveals | repairs | supersedes | depends-on)
concepts.meaning: An explicit, attributable, typed link between two durable records with evidence; never inferred from time, paths or Git co-presence; traversed both ways for navigation.
concepts.overlap_note: Scope also has generic `relations` between assets (contains, anchors, …) which are not consequences.

concepts.name: reference (kind:id)
aliases: decision:… | work:… | commit:… | experiment:… | verification:… | defect:…
concepts.meaning: The addressing form for durable records; commits check against Git, ledger ids against their strict readers; a free-form legacy label remains navigable history but cannot clear work.

concepts.name: orient heading
aliases: refuse | await-human | resolve-conflict | repair-navigation | unblock | synthesize | dispatch | continue | verify | steady
concepts.meaning: One deterministic next action selected in fixed priority over the strict ledgers (work, decisions, consequences, experiments, defects, verification); it never runs the action and grants no authority.
concepts.overlap_note: Overlaps with `regulate`, which also emits 'exactly one next action' from a different rule set.

concepts.name: regulator
concepts.meaning: A narrow control loop over live readings that applies the versioned doctrine and emits at most one executable intervention; release means only that no rule fired.
concepts.overlap_note: Two 'one next action' machines (orient, regulate) with different inputs and priorities.

concepts.name: doctrine
concepts.meaning: The small versioned registry of rules the regulator may apply, each with a live observation and a remedy; order is API and cannot be configured.
concepts.overlap_note: 'doctrine' is also used loosely in prose for the project's philosophy (dissolve > declare > infer).

concepts.name: host
concepts.meaning: The agent runtime whose lifecycle files coherence owns (.claude/settings.json or .codex/hooks.json); one lifecycle contract, two host syntaxes, independent controls.

concepts.name: swarm roles
concepts.meaning: The cast the coordination layer names: orchestrators/coordinators create and hand off work, owners advance exact assignments, assessors author consequence edges and experiment closes, peers' entries are claims to assess.

concepts.name: live canary / efficacy trial
concepts.meaning: README's protocol for validating a swarm: a predeclared canary proves mechanisms (attribution, collision sensing, handoff, synthesis, recovery) in one host; a matched trial asks whether they help.
defined_in: README.md#Validate a swarm in the field
concepts.overlap_note: 'canary' also names the serial runner canary and the PostToolUse dependency canary.

concepts.name: lifecycle control
aliases: hooks install / uninstall / status / print / review / --check
concepts.meaning: One immutable, host-selected hook bundle plus stable launcher and root mapping; presence is a single canonical runnable bit (exactly one shared copy, no competing path, runnable target).
concepts.overlap_note: The spec says 'six-event value', the README 'five event names' — the count itself is spelled two ways.

concepts.name: hook events
concepts.meaning: The host events the bundle wires: starts open a session and inject instructions, PostToolUse traces paths and delivers the feed, SubagentStop nudges once, main Stop snapshots calibration silently.

concepts.name: hook body
concepts.meaning: The dependency-light executable the harness invokes per event; its meaning is versioned (protocol 8 today) so an event from an older wire cannot prove the new body ran.

concepts.name: activation
aliases: structural presence vs current-session activation vs historical observation
concepts.meaning: Three different facts the control reports: the bundle is installed; this exact session's activity names this host, launcher transport and bundle fingerprint; hooks fired in the past.

concepts.name: attribution ceiling
concepts.meaning: Codex PostToolUse carries no agent_id, so descendant activity lands in the parent's file; rows are kept but labeled aggregate and never promoted to exact child evidence.
concepts.overlap_note: Same idea as telemetry scope; spelled at three sites (hooks status, experiment close, calibration).

concepts.name: agent instructions
concepts.meaning: The byte-testable text injected at every session/subagent start teaching the journal verbs, orient/work loop, guarantee links, conjecture, defect, experiment, escalate; part of the versioned hook protocol.

concepts.name: assigned work instructions
aliases: owner menu (start | block | finish | resume | yield | cancel | handoff)
concepts.meaning: SessionStart's rendering of up to three work orders owned by exactly this session, with only the lifecycle commands valid for their state, each carrying the predecessor token.

concepts.name: project voice
concepts.meaning: Per-event project files that replace or follow the canonical hook emission; damage degrades to canon, and `hooks review` prints effective emissions with provenance.
defined_in: README.md#The project's voice in the emissions

concepts.name: stop feedback
concepts.meaning: SubagentStop restates the report plus journal count and patch signal once; main Stop emits nothing so a shared worktree cannot become one agent's obligation.

concepts.name: due
concepts.meaning: A SessionStart section naming which recorded instruments (verify full tier, drift, economy, …) have not run in N commits; reads only, writes nothing, silent when nothing is due.

concepts.name: reading surface
aliases: owned block / fenced block / marker pair
concepts.meaning: What humans and agents read: HTML renders, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md's owned block, README's derived blocks, terminal reports; derived from the graph, it can mislead but cannot turn red green.

concepts.name: derived spelling
aliases: derive one spelling from the other
concepts.meaning: The doctrine and its instances: a registry is the single home and the banner, README index and phrasebook table are pure functions of it, byte-compared by `docs --check`.

concepts.name: freshness gate (--check)
concepts.meaning: Regenerate in memory and compare with the committed artifact, normalizing volatile fields (timestamps, absolute path, line numbers) except for pure-function blocks compared byte-for-byte.
concepts.overlap_note: 'freshness' here is artifact staleness, unrelated to verdict freshness.

concepts.name: outline
concepts.meaning: The navigable outline of the derived graph, written by `coherence graph`.

concepts.name: overview / agent map
concepts.meaning: The generated component map (intent, why, works when, files) plus folder tree and dictionary, for agents (markdown) and humans (HTML).

concepts.name: CLAUDE.md block
concepts.meaning: The one generated region inside an authored CLAUDE.md: component map and the boundary-derived invariants table; everything outside stays authored.

concepts.name: contract (promise graph)
concepts.meaning: The reading of a project's obligations: components making guarantees at perimeters (gates) and relying on one another's (reliances), graded and placed on declared trust walls; always regenerated, no --check.
concepts.overlap_note: 'contract' is also the `contracts` ratchet (producer/consumer), conventions' 'contract vs convention', and the trust-ladder word 'promote conventions to contracts'.

concepts.name: gate
concepts.meaning: The promise graph's atomic promise: one boundary claim rendered with its grade, crossing and reliants. Also used generically for 'a check that can fail the build'.
concepts.overlap_note: Duplicate of boundary claim/invariant at the render layer; also 'gate' vs 'advisory' vs 'ratchet' as command classes.

concepts.name: grade
concepts.meaning: A total function of a gate's one recorded claim signal and verb: A fresh via-test pass, B stale pass, C via-guard pass, D no effective pass, U dialect-gap skip (rendered ink, never blank).
concepts.overlap_note: 'grade' is also used for evidence grades of instruments ('direct-file grade', 'direct-module grade', catalog example grade) — a different, informal sense.

concepts.name: reliance
concepts.meaning: In the promise graph, every cross-component import is a reliance: covered by a gate on the wall it crosses or naked; every gate lists its reliants. Structure instead draws only declared `relies on` links as amber tabs.
concepts.overlap_note: Two 'reliance' populations: derived-from-imports (promise graph, Scope `reliance` asset) and declared (`## relies on`, Scope `guarantee-link`/`relies` relation).

concepts.name: mass
aliases: dimensions (lines|total, lines|<component>, files|total, symbols|total, deps|direct/dev/transitive, measure|<key>)
concepts.meaning: How much machine there is, pinned: the growth ratchet over lines, files, symbols, dependencies and project probes whose failure prescribes `coherence decide`; also the promise graph's per-component line denominator.
concepts.overlap_note: 'mass' means both the ratchet's dimensions and the promise graph's accounted/unaccounted lines and Scope's `attributes.mass.total` graph weight.

concepts.name: measures
concepts.meaning: Project-declared commands whose last numeric stdout token becomes a mass dimension; a nonzero exit or no number is unmeasurable and fails --check, never 0.

concepts.name: index
concepts.meaning: Three views for a returning human framed against what they last saw: the map (components, zones, gates, crossings, trust), the journal (blocked first, open conjectures, decisions) and the trajectory (invariant-set diff, LOC, mass and drift trends). Derives nothing new.
concepts.overlap_note: 'index' is also the static oracle index and Git's index.

concepts.name: four darknesses
concepts.meaning: The index's four never-merged measures of what is not known: invariants without refutations, files no claim names, symbols without docblocks, and paths recent work touches that the graph does not own.

concepts.name: panel
concepts.meaning: A zero-dependency terminal view over the graph and the status record with honesty rules for lights (stale, not run, dialect gap, human-eye); it spawns the CLI rather than re-running anything in-process.
defined_in: README.md#The status record and the panel

concepts.name: context packet
concepts.meaning: The smallest useful reading for a task: ownership, intent/why, invariants, chokepoints, one-hop imports, relevant tests, repository surfaces, standing decisions and open conjectures, bounded to 12,000 bytes with every withheld item and byte named.
concepts.overlap_note: 'context' also means the experiment's predicted context and the claim evaluation ctx.

concepts.name: Scope
concepts.meaning: The configurable reading surface over the whole asset catalog (structure, specs, guarantees, work, journal, taxonomy, evidence, hooks): offline HTML or a read-only live server; views are data, never code.
concepts.overlap_note: 'scope' collides with verify scope, work scopes and decision scope fields.

concepts.name: asset
concepts.meaning: Scope's transport unit: every canonical record adapted once into an addressable asset with a kind, a reader's label, a source and its full attributes, plus explicit relations between assets.
concepts.overlap_note: Asset kinds re-spell nearly every concept in this list (`guarantee`, `reliance`, `chart`, `zone`, `instrument`, …) as presentation ids.

concepts.name: view
aliases: kinds / where / sort / fields / groupBy / pageSize
field format (text | json | count | date | list | prose | session | taxonomy | excerpt | kind | grade)
default views (structure, guarantees, specs, work, journal, taxonomy, obligations, evidence, hooks, assets)
concepts.meaning: A declarative selection and presentation of assets; shipped defaults and project views use the same language and refuse unknown keys.

concepts.name: Structure
concepts.meaning: Scope's first default view: component cards ranked by spec density and declared reliance, connected only by spec-owned architectural relationships and declared guarantee reliance; imports never draw arrows and files never become cards.
concepts.overlap_note: Not the 'Structure graph' of decompose (the import graph) nor the AGENTS.md '## Structure' folder tree — three 'Structure's.

concepts.name: card
aliases: card variant (component stack | guarantee | entrance/boundary | resource)
concepts.meaning: Structure's visual unit for a component (and, in the thesis, for guarantees, entrances and resources); zoom changes detail within fixed rectangles.

concepts.name: stack
concepts.meaning: The thesis's main visual unit: a closed stack outlines a component, opening it reveals architectural cards and local relationships; the shipped Structure retired on-map unfurling as 'chart theatrics'.
concepts.overlap_note: A stack is a component at the presentation layer; the word survives in docs after the mechanism was retired.

concepts.name: inspector / reading
concepts.meaning: The Scope column that explains a selected asset or connection: one reading per subject kind (identity, meaning, participants, evidence, rationale, provenance) rendered from data blocks.
concepts.overlap_note: 'reading' is also every instrument's output ('a reading the graph already took') and the atlas's 'reading-surface' chart.

concepts.name: source availability
concepts.meaning: Scope's independent report of whether each canonical reader could be read; a failed source loses its whole contribution and stays visible outside filters so absence never reads as health.

concepts.name: Scope extension
aliases: named implementation (rankers | layouts | routers | cards | views)
concepts.meaning: Versioned project modules bundled at generation time that replace ranking, placement, routing, card content or the whole Structure view while inheriting defaults; executable project code, not configuration.

concepts.name: comparison (planned)
concepts.meaning: Thesis-level requirements not yet implemented: comparing two compatible asset snapshots with retained removals, and an MCP surface for agents to direct Scope.
concepts.overlap_note: Overlaps the implemented `log` ledger (invariant-set diff) and the index trajectory.

concepts.name: advisory
concepts.meaning: The class of instruments that report ranked, capped findings and never change the exit code (redundancy, prose, why-lint, decompose, drift, economy, premise, calibrate, novelty, never-red).
concepts.overlap_note: Contrast class to 'gate' and 'ratchet'.

concepts.name: --raise
concepts.meaning: Opt-in flag letting an advisory (verify, redundancy, mass, atlas, economy) open conjectures in the journal keyed on the finding's subject instead of printing them; capped per run and the remainder announced.

concepts.name: finding key
concepts.meaning: The identity a raised or attested finding carries: the addressable subject and nothing volatile (no score, count or line number), so a question is not re-minted every run.

concepts.name: ratchet
concepts.meaning: An instrument that pins a reading to a baseline and fails --check on new or grown entries while shrinkage never fails; the mechanism is the harness's, the data the project's.
concepts.overlap_note: README also calls the unanchored-invariant coverage gate 'the ratchet' and the boundary machinery 'the anti-entropy ratchet'.

concepts.name: baseline
concepts.meaning: A ratchet's memory of a reading it once took; keyed sites are reconciled across renames without absorbing growth or duplication, and an empty reading is refused over a live pin.
concepts.overlap_note: Also the `--baseline` number in `observed` and 'clean baseline' in the canary protocol.

concepts.name: atlas
concepts.meaning: The project-declared map of trust domains and the chokepoints crossing between them, each crossing graded by tier from live claims plus explicit enshrinement, with heat and inference hazards.
concepts.overlap_note: Atlas 'drift' (mapped symbol moved) is unrelated to the `drift` command (architectural direction).

concepts.name: chart
aliases: project-source | derived-model | shell | record | verdict | reading-surface
concepts.meaning: A trust domain in the atlas (config `atlas.charts`), described in prose; this repo declares six for the harness itself.
concepts.overlap_note: A chart is a trust region declared in config; a zone is a trust region declared in the entry spec — two homes for one idea.

concepts.name: transition
aliases: from / to / translates / security / anchoredBy / enshrined
concepts.meaning: A chokepoint symbol that crosses between two charts and what it translates; `nonTransition` records symbols that hold within a chart, `knownPending` tolerates mapped symbols not yet in source.
concepts.overlap_note: Re-spells the claim-level `crossing <zone> -> <zone>` in config with chart names instead of zone names.

concepts.name: tier (enforcement ladder)
aliases: tier-1 enshrined | tier-2 totality-checked | tier-3 convention
concepts.meaning: Where a rule sits: unrepresentable by construction (type system), one home plus a totality oracle (what boundary claims target), or N sites held by memory. The atlas grades every crossing on it; the README reads the same ladder as price and as trust.
defined_in: README.md#The mental model: the enforcement ladder
concepts.overlap_note: Third 'tier' vocabulary (see verify run tier, claim tier).

concepts.name: heat
concepts.meaning: The share of recent concern-carrying commits touching the file that defines a chokepoint (or symbol); a temperature that grades nothing, used to rank crossings, doc jobs and inference hazards.

concepts.name: inference hazard
concepts.meaning: The join of undeclared (tier-3) and busy (hot): a place where every reader re-derives what may legally cross; raised as a conjecture keyed on the symbol.

concepts.name: convention / guard
concepts.meaning: A guard function reached at more than one call site with no enforcing contract (anchored boundary or totality test) — a block-list that fails open; the detector ratchets the unguarded set.
concepts.overlap_note: 'guard' here (a function) vs `via guard` (an oracle verb) vs 'gate' — three near-synonyms.

concepts.name: sink
concepts.meaning: A raw interpolation into a dangerous context; the ratchet baselines reviewed sites, reconciles moves, and fails --check on a new one; safe-by-construction patterns are project config.
concepts.overlap_note: 'site' is also redundancy's unit (a spelled-out domain).

concepts.name: data contract (contracts command)
concepts.meaning: A declared typed message emitted at one chokepoint and consumed at another across deploy units, resolved against the graph and graded anchored iff a boundary/parity claim names one of its symbols; plus a detector for undeclared shared vocabulary.
concepts.overlap_note: Second meaning of 'contract' (the first is the promise graph render; conventions.ts uses a third, 'contract vs convention').

concepts.name: deploy artifact
concepts.meaning: A named compile/deploy unit declared as path globs so cross-unit contracts can be located; a file may belong to several.
concepts.overlap_note: 'artifact' also means generated reading-surface artifacts (`writesArtifacts`) and receipt artifacts (input manifests).

concepts.name: novelty
aliases: surface (net-new exports, union/enum variants, keyed-table keys, LOC)
concepts.meaning: After the structural ledger, contrast behavioral surface added across a ref range with anchors added; significant surface with zero anchors raises the alarm, self-qualified when churn dominates.
concepts.overlap_note: The index also uses 'novelty' for 'is this finding news since the cursor' — a different sense.

concepts.name: signal
concepts.meaning: The gate over novelty: significant surface with zero new invariant/boundary/parity anchors and no patch-fingerprinted decision reds under --check; the escape hatch is a journal decision, not a config switch.
concepts.overlap_note: 'signal' is also the taxonomy question namespace (`signal:invocation`) — unrelated.

concepts.name: log / structural ledger
concepts.meaning: The diff of the invariant/boundary/parity/component set between two refs, built from a throwaway worktree at each ref; a loss fails --strict.
concepts.overlap_note: README calls this 'the ledger' as it also calls the journal, the work ledger, the reliance ledger and the maintenance-cost ledger.

concepts.name: redundancy
aliases: site (union | enum | interface members | Record keys | switch cases | === chain | string array | markdown table column | a|b|c alternation)
concepts.meaning: The detector for the same set of tokens written out at two sites with nothing tying them together; compiler-enforced pairs are collapsed, declared parity pairs dropped, and drifted pairs rank first.

concepts.name: prose rot
concepts.meaning: Sentences cached in two reading surfaces (README, release notes, specs, module headers) that share six-word shingles; divergence ranks first because it is rot no reader can see from one copy.

concepts.name: why-lint
concepts.meaning: Two advisories on rationale: prose that restates a boundary's mechanism, and, in invariant-bearing specs, paragraphs and invariants that do not anchor each other by name.

concepts.name: decompose
aliases: smells (false-boundary, smeared concern, missing abstraction, structure hub)
concepts.meaning: Measures agreement between the spec tree, the import graph and git co-change; prints a LOCALITY score plus the smells that lower it; advisory.

concepts.name: locality / spread
concepts.meaning: Locality: the fraction of pairwise co-change that stays inside one component (rising = wiser); spread: distinct components per commit (falling = localizing).

concepts.name: drift
concepts.meaning: Projects today's component map over recent history and shows whether the codebase is converging or decohering, with the boundary being churned now and the recent gesture stream; prunes are excluded.
concepts.overlap_note: Word collision: atlas 'drift' (a mapped symbol moved), docs 'drift' (stale artifact), narrative 'drifted' statement, and 'behavioural drift' in prose.

concepts.name: economy (context closure)
concepts.meaning: The read side of the work ledger: per commit, the touched graph files plus direct import neighbours in both directions plus their spec files; reported as trend, worst closures and hubs; always exits 0.
concepts.overlap_note: 'economy' is also the README's whole doctrine ('the economy of inference').

concepts.name: economy of inference
aliases: trust is the license to skip inference
concepts.meaning: The governing model: the expensive resource is inference, paid again by every reader; coherence moves facts down the ladder from inferred to read to unaskable, and the enforcement ladder is the same ladder priced.
defined_in: README.md#The same ladder, read as trust

concepts.name: metaphor vocabulary
concepts.meaning: The recurring images the README and module headers use to explain instruments; each is bound to one concept (label=claim, breaker trip=refutation, blower door=totality oracle, gyroscope=orient, thermostat=decompose).
defined_in: README.md#The same ladder, read as trust
concepts.overlap_note: Not concepts themselves, but names a reader meets in prose and must map back.

concepts.name: judge ≠ notary
aliases: the right claims vs passing claims
concepts.meaning: The harness records verdicts mechanically but never judges whether a claim is the right claim; a spec full of green trivialities is coherent and worthless.

concepts.name: damage
concepts.meaning: Surviving evidence that cannot be trusted; every strict reader treats it as counted damage that makes the population unavailable rather than silently smaller.

concepts.name: taxonomy
concepts.meaning: Evidence-addressed classification of files and symbols into roles and facets by answering signal questions; only `record` writes, every suggestion stays unverified, and history reads against the catalog version it captured.

concepts.name: role
concepts.meaning: A responsibility a component can be assessed as fulfilling (cli-orchestrator, registry-authority, parser, validator-type-checker, …); selected only on positive operational signals, never by name cues.

concepts.name: facet
concepts.meaning: A cross-cutting property (boundary, deterministic, persistence, observability, lifecycle, …) assessed independently of role and never treated as an exhaustive checklist.

concepts.name: signal question
concepts.meaning: The yes/no/unknown questions whose positive answers propose roles; unanswered or unknown is not a negative observation.
concepts.overlap_note: Namespace `signal:` collides in prose with the `signal` command.

concepts.name: assessment
aliases: status (unassessed | needs-evidence | no-fit | ambiguous | classified | composite)
concepts.meaning: An immutable, content-addressed, predecessor-addressed record of one caller-assessed classification with its inputs, evidence and freshness snapshot; the current view is rebuilt from them.

concepts.name: subject
aliases: freshness scope (whole file, direct imports, evidence, manifests)
concepts.meaning: One graph-resolved file or exported symbol whose bytes and direct dependencies are hashed so an assessment can expire when they change.
concepts.overlap_note: 'subject' is also a coverage claim's subject, a decision's --subject, a raised finding's subject and Scope's 'subject kind'.

concepts.name: command registry
aliases: command group (derive | verify | journal | perceive | ratchet | advisory | bootstrap | reference)
concepts.meaning: The one declarative home of the 51 verbs, their groups, arg shapes and flags; the banner and README index derive from it and a test asserts it equals the live dispatch.

concepts.name: command groups
aliases: Verify, and diff what is enforced
concepts.meaning: The eight families the CLI surface is organised into; also the informal classes gate / ratchet / advisory / journal used across prose.

concepts.name: scaffold
concepts.meaning: Generators that emit the complete anti-entropic anatomy (spec + invariants + boundary claim + oracle skeleton) so the convergent shape is the cheapest thing to ship.

concepts.name: exit code contract
concepts.meaning: Across commands: 0 means held/released/advisory, 1 means a gate failed, 2 means the instrument could not answer safely (damaged evidence, invalid config, usage error).

concepts.name: instrument
concepts.meaning: The project's word for any measuring command; its output is a 'reading', and 'doubt the instrument before the subject' is the injected first hypothesis of every conjecture.

concepts.name: the field
concepts.meaning: Prose name for the state a running lifecycle control plus ledgers establish around agents (instructions injected, journal written, work visible); an absent control 'cannot create a field'.

concepts.name: assay
concepts.meaning: Recorded external exercises of the harness against reference projects (PostHog, Mnemion) that produced the guarantee catalog, adoption readiness data and field reports.

concepts.name: prune
concepts.meaning: A commit with more deletions than insertions; excluded from drift's trajectory and drawn as a negative bar in mass, because deletion must stay free.

concepts.name: artifact ownership
concepts.meaning: Which files coherence owns wholly (graph.json, HTML renders, AGENTS.md, promise.json, atlas.md), which are two-zone (CLAUDE.md, README.md), and which stay authored.

concepts.name: sidecar scan
concepts.meaning: The shared file scan the ratchets use, scoped by `config.sources` and split by `testDir`, deliberately not `config.ignore` because the conventions lint needs test files.
concepts.overlap_note: Two ignore lists (`ignore` for the graph, NOISE_DIRS for scans and oracle hunting) were themselves a redundancy finding this repo dismissed.

suspected_duplicates.why: One authored invariant anchored by one boundary claim is rendered as a gate by the promise graph, hashed as a g-… guarantee by guarantees.ts/Scope, and titled 'Invariants' in the Scope Guarantees view — four names, one thing, no decision choosing.
Both are declared trust regions between which chokepoints cross; zones live in the entry spec, charts in config, and docs/scope.md has to remind readers they are 'different concepts'.
A claim's `crossing a -> b` and a config `atlas.transitions[symbol] {from,to}` both say which trust regions a chokepoint separates, spelled twice with different region vocabularies.
Four kinds of 'A depends on B' arrows: derived import reliance (promise graph), declared `## relies on` links, spec-owned relationships (Structure handoffs), and raw import edges.
Two machines each promise 'exactly one deterministic next action' over overlapping ledgers with separate rule sets and priority orders.
'tier' names fast/full runs, deterministic/live/executable/hybrid forms, and the enshrined/totality-checked/convention ladder — three unrelated scales under one word.
Taxonomy-suggested obligations, a proposed spec section, and regulator obligations (a rule owed an action) all use 'obligation'.
Catalog definitions (`guarantee:scoped-reads`) and taxonomy suggestions (`guarantee:G-…`) share the `guarantee:` id namespace but are declared incompatible populations.
'contract' means the promise-graph render, a producer/consumer data contract, and the opposite of a convention in the ladder.
The `coverage` verb (an open-domain claim with a residual) and verify's coverage gate (claims present, invariants anchored, why present) share a name and a report line.
A journal `blocked` row (history, no close) and a `blocked` work state (live scheduler) look alike and orient had to be taught to treat them differently.
Both record verify results; receipts exist because the merged status cannot identify one run, leaving two overlapping evidence stores.
The same none/owner-session/parent-session-aggregate/legacy-unscoped vocabulary is spelled at hook status, experiment close and calibration.
'journal' names the record, the live command, the Scope view and the peer feed; 'decisions' names a read command and the folder holding all nine record kinds.
'drift' is the architectural-direction command, an atlas --check failure class, an artifact staleness word and a narrative statement state.
'Structure' names the Scope renderer, decompose's import graph, and the AGENTS.md folder-tree section.
A component at the presentation layer is called a stack (retired unfurl mechanism), a card (shipped), and an organ (index).
